oligos.target_gene: TTR (transthyretin); human transthyretin nucleic acid SEQ ID NO: 1 = GENBANK NM_000371.2
oligos.indication: Transthyretin amyloidosis / transthyretin-related disease (the patent's stated therapeutic use)
oligos.sequence_locus: Table 4 ('Inhibition of human transthyretin mRNA levels by chimeric antisense oligonucleotides targeted to SEQ ID NO: 1'), row *304299, Sequence column - US9061044.txt line 6045; the same sequence is designated SEQ ID NO: 25.
oligos.gapmer_design: 5-10-5 MOE gapmer (5 nt 2'-MOE wing / 10 nt 2'-deoxy gap / 5 nt 2'-MOE wing), stated as 'Motif' 5-10-5 in Table 4
oligos.ps_count: 19 (all 19 internucleoside linkages of this 20-mer; derived from the explicit statement 'The internucleoside linkages throughout each gapmer are phosphorothioate (P=S) linkages', not from a printed count)
oligos.notes: Chemistry is not printed per-position next to this compound; it is fixed by the Table 4 design legend (US9061044.txt line 5801): "The 5-10-5 gapmers are 20 nucleotides in length, wherein the central gap segment is comprised of ten 2'-deoxynucleotides and is flanked on both sides (in the 5' and 3' directions) by wings comprising five nucleotides each... each nucleotide in the 5' wing segment and each nucleotide in the 3' wing segment has a 2'-MOE modification. Independent claim 1 (line 722) states the same design for SEQ ID NO: 80. Target start/stop sites 507-526 are on SEQ ID NO: 1 (GENBANK NM_000371.2, human TTR), per the Table 4 column headers. No purity, analytical method, identity confirmation or synthesis platform is reported anywhere in this patent for any compound; all CMC fields are genuine reporting silence, not omissions by the curator.

measurements.system_model: Male cynomolgus monkey (Macaca fascicularis), repeat-dose 12-week efficacy/tolerability study, Example 24
measurements.delivery_method: subcutaneous injection, thrice per week for the first week then twice per week for the next 11 weeks
measurements.exposure_duration: 12 weeks of repeat subcutaneous dosing (3x/week week 1, then 2x/week for 11 weeks); the study day on which this 0-48 h time course was run is NOT_REPORTED
measurements.control_description: PBS vehicle control group (4 cynomolgus monkeys, same subcutaneous schedule), same table, same 0 hr column
measurements.effect_vs_control: +0.30 s vs the PBS group at the same 0 hr timepoint (10.38 vs 10.08); ratio to PBS 1.03-fold
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: As shown in Tables 86-88, PT, aPTT and fibrinogen were not significantly altered in monkeys treated with ISIS oligonucleotides compared to the PBS control.
measurements.source_locus: US 9,061,044 B2, Example 24, subsection 'Coagulation Tests', Table 86 ('Effect of antisense oligonucleotide treatment on PT (sec)'), row 'ISIS 304299', column '0 hr' (PBS row at US9061044.txt line 18600; compound row at line 18609)
measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 86 | Effect of antisense oligonucleotide treatment on PT (sec) | 0 hr 1 hr 4 hr 8 hr 24 hr 48 hr | PBS 10.08 10.38 10.10 10.33 9.83 9.40 | ISIS 304299 10.38 10.30 10.48 10.20 9.95 9.53
measurements.notes: Group mean as printed; the patent prints no SD, SEM, n-per-timepoint or statistical test for Tables 86-88, so 'increase'/'decrease' describes the sign of the difference between the two printed group means only and carries no claim of statistical significance. CONTRADICTION: the prose immediately above these tables asserts that PT, aPTT and fibrinogen were not significantly altered. For aPTT (Table 87) and for fibrinogen (Table 88) in the 420921/420922/420950/420957/420959 groups the printed table values contradict that assertion. The prose claim is preserved verbatim in severity_stated_by_source on every row. PT differences here are small (all within about 1 second of the PBS group) and are the one readout in this example for which the prose null claim looks consistent with the printed numbers; direction is still recorded from the printed values rather than being rounded to no_change, because the patent supplies no variance with which to justify calling it a null. Study day of this 0-48 h time course is NOT stated. The patent says only that PT and aPTT were measured 'over a period of 48 hrs'. Terminal sacrifice was on day 86, 48 hours after the last dose, so a time course anchored on the final dose is plausible - but the patent does not say so and this has NOT been assumed. The '0 hr' column is likewise not defined as pre-dose. Note that the 0 hr values already separate the groups (e.g. Table 87, ISIS 420957 29.13 s vs PBS 19.40 s at 0 hr), which is consistent with the time course being run after weeks of repeat dosing rather than after a single first dose.

measurements.notes: Group mean as printed; the patent prints no SD, SEM, n-per-timepoint or statistical test for Tables 86-88, so 'increase'/'decrease' describes the sign of the difference between the two printed group means only and carries no claim of statistical significance. CONTRADICTION: the prose immediately above these tables asserts that PT, aPTT and fibrinogen were not significantly altered. For aPTT (Table 87) and for fibrinogen (Table 88) in the 420921/420922/420950/420957/420959 groups the printed table values contradict that assertion. The prose claim is preserved verbatim in severity_stated_by_source on every row. PT differences here are small (all within about 1 second of the PBS group) and are the one readout in this example for which the prose null claim looks consistent with the printed numbers; direction is still recorded from the printed values rather than being rounded to no_change, because the patent supplies no variance with which to justify calling it a null. Study day of this 0-48 h time course is NOT stated. The patent says only that PT and aPTT were measured 'over a period of 48 hrs'. Terminal sacrifice was on day 86, 48 hours after the last dose, so a time course anchored on the final dose is plausible - but the patent does not say so and this has NOT been assumed. The '0 hr' column is likewise not defined as pre-dose. Note that the 0 hr values already separate the groups (e.g. Table 87, ISIS 420957 29.13 s vs PBS 19.40 s at 0 hr), which is consistent with the time course being run after weeks of repeat dosing rather than after a single first dose.

measurements.verbatim_quote: TABLE 88 | Effect of antisense oligonucleotide treatment on fibrinogen (mg/dL) | 0 hr 1 hr 4 hr 8 hr 24 hr 48 hr | PBS 212 203 240 247 282 272 | ISIS 420921 208 209 230 237 301 249
measurements.notes: Group mean as printed; the patent prints no SD, SEM, n-per-timepoint or statistical test for Tables 86-88, so 'increase'/'decrease' describes the sign of the difference between the two printed group means only and carries no claim of statistical significance. CONTRADICTION: the prose immediately above these tables asserts that PT, aPTT and fibrinogen were not significantly altered. For aPTT (Table 87) and for fibrinogen (Table 88) in the 420921/420922/420950/420957/420959 groups the printed table values contradict that assertion. The prose claim is preserved verbatim in severity_stated_by_source on every row. Fibrinogen is an acute-phase reactant; this row is reported here as a coagulation-panel readout as the patent presents it, without any attribution of mechanism. Study day of this 0-48 h time course is NOT stated. The patent says only that PT and aPTT were measured 'over a period of 48 hrs'. Terminal sacrifice was on day 86, 48 hours after the last dose, so a time course anchored on the final dose is plausible - but the patent does not say so and this has NOT been assumed. The '0 hr' column is likewise not defined as pre-dose. Note that the 0 hr values already separate the groups (e.g. Table 87, ISIS 420957 29.13 s vs PBS 19.40 s at 0 hr), which is consistent with the time course being run after weeks of repeat dosing rather than after a single first dose.

extraction_notes:
SCOPE. Coagulation data in US 9,061,044 B2 exist in exactly one place: Example 24 (12-week repeat-dose cynomolgus monkey study), subsection 'Coagulation Tests', Tables 86 (PT, sec), 87 (aPTT, sec) and 88 (fibrinogen, mg/dL). A case-insensitive sweep of the whole 437,109-byte file for aPTT / prothrombin / coagulation / clotting / thrombin / fibrinogen / bleeding / haemorrhage / D-dimer / antithrombin found no other coagulation readout. The mouse and rat tolerability examples (11, 13, 17, 18, 19, 23) report hematology and serum chemistry panels but NO clotting times - that is reporting silence for this endpoint in the rodent work and has not been converted into rows.

PRIMARY CURATION FINDING - PROSE/TABLE CONTRADICTION. The paragraph introducing the tables (US9061044.txt line 18569) states verbatim: 'As shown in Tables 86-88, PT, aPTT and fibrinogen were not significantly altered in monkeys treated with ISIS oligonucleotides compared to the PBS control.' The tables it points to do not support that claim for aPTT. Table 87 shows a clean compound rank order of aPTT prolongation at every one of the six timepoints, peaking at 4-8 h: at 4 h PBS is 20.13 s while ISIS 420957 is 39.13 s (+19.00 s, 1.94-fold), ISIS 420950 35.40 s (1.76-fold), ISIS 420922 34.83 s (1.73-fold), ISIS 420921 31.78 s (1.58-fold), ISIS 420959 29.18 s (1.45-fold), ISIS 304299 27.05 s (1.34-fold) and ISIS 420915 23.83 s (1.18-fold). Every ISIS group exceeds PBS at every timepoint in Table 87. Any pipeline that reads the abstract or the summary sentence rather than the tables records a false negative here. Extraction was done from the tables; the prose sentence is preserved verbatim in severity_stated_by_source on all 126 numeric rows so the contradiction travels with the data instead of being resolved silently by the curator.

SECOND CONTRADICTION, BEYOND THE TRIAGE NOTE. The same 'not significantly altered' sentence also covers fibrinogen, and Table 88 contradicts it too - which the triage note did not flag. At 24 h, PBS fibrinogen is 282 mg/dL while ISIS 420957 is 434 (1.54-fold), ISIS 420959 414 (1.47-fold), ISIS 420922 400 (1.42-fold) and ISIS 420950 390 (1.38-fold). The direction is not uniform: ISIS 304299 runs BELOW PBS at every timepoint (e.g. 227 vs 282 at 24 h) and ISIS 420915 is mixed. Notably, the four compounds with the largest fibrinogen elevations are also the four with the longest aPTT, so the two tables are rank-concordant. Fibrinogen is an acute-phase reactant and the patent offers no mechanism; no mechanistic interpretation has been added to the rows. Table 86 (PT) is the one readout where the prose null claim looks consistent with the numbers - all groups sit within about 1 s of PBS - although ISIS 420957 is above PBS at all six timepoints there as well.

DIRECTION RULE (applied uniformly, no thresholds). effect_direction is the sign of (printed group mean minus printed PBS mean) at the SAME timepoint column; 'no_change' would be used only for identical printed values, and no row in these tables is identical. The patent prints no SD, SEM, per-timepoint n or statistical test for Tables 86-88, so 'increase'/'decrease' is a description of two printed means and asserts nothing about significance. effect_vs_control carries the arithmetic difference and the ratio, both computed from the printed values only, so that central grading can apply its own rubric. No severity grade has been assigned by this extraction.

PARSING HAZARDS. (1) The file is an HTML-to-text conversion in which every table cell sits on its own line with leading whitespace, so table rows have no single contiguous line to quote. verbatim_quote therefore reproduces the table number, the caption, the timepoint header, the PBS row and the compound row as exact tokens joined by single spaces - the tokens are verbatim, the whitespace is normalized, and this is the only transformation applied. Every row also carries the exact source line numbers in source_locus so a reviewer can re-read the raw block. (2) Tables 86-88 were parsed programmatically (locate the 'TABLE n' line, assert the header is exactly 0 hr / 1 hr / 4 hr / 8 hr / 24 hr / 48 hr, then read label + 6 numeric cells per row) and the parse was cross-checked against a manual read of the same block; no value was hand-transcribed. (3) The file uses the Unicode micro sign in other tables; irrelevant here but it defeats an ASCII 'uM' grep elsewhere in the document.

STUDY-DAY GAP - IMPORTANT. The study day on which the 0-48 h coagulation time course was run is NOT stated. The patent says only that PT and aPTT were 'measured using platelet poor plasma (PPP) from the monkeys over a period of 48 hrs'. Terminal sacrifice was on day 86, 48 hours after the last dose, which makes a time course anchored on the final dose plausible, but the patent never says so and this extraction has NOT assumed it. Consistent with a late-study time course, the '0 hr' values already separate the groups (Table 87: ISIS 420957 29.13 s vs PBS 19.40 s at 0 hr), so '0 hr' is very unlikely to be a treatment-naive baseline; the patent does not define it as pre-dose. Anyone using the 0 hr column as a baseline should treat that as an assumption of their own.

n PER GROUP. Groups were four monkeys as randomized. One ISIS 420957 monkey was withdrawn on day 44 and one ISIS 420950 monkey on day 76, both for illness, so the n behind those two groups' coagulation means may be 3 rather than 4; the tables do not state per-timepoint n. n_subjects is recorded as '4' (the randomized group size) with the caveat repeated in the notes of the affected rows.

MISSING COMPOUND. Eight ASOs were dosed but only seven appear in Tables 86-88. ISIS 420955 is absent because its entire group was withdrawn on day 31 for illness. Three explicit reporting-silence rows (PT, aPTT, fibrinogen) carry ISIS 420955 with readout_value NOT_REPORTED and effect_direction NOT_REPORTED so that this gap is distinguishable from a measured null. The patent does not attribute any of the illness withdrawals (ISIS 420955 group day 31, one ISIS 420957 animal day 44, one ISIS 420950 animal day 76) to a coagulation cause, and no such attribution has been inferred - but a reviewer should note that the two single-animal withdrawals came from the two groups with the longest aPTT and among the highest fibrinogen.

PBS ROWS. The PBS vehicle group is not represented as an oligo and has no rows of its own; its values appear as control_value on all 126 compound rows, which preserves every printed PBS number.

CHEMISTRY / modifications ARRAY. This patent does not use a per-position case convention. It does, however, print an explicit positional design legend for Table 4 (US9061044.txt line 5801) - 5-10-5 gapmer, wings of five 2'-MOE nucleosides each side, ten 2'-deoxynucleotide gap, 'The internucleoside linkages throughout each gapmer are phosphorothioate (P=S) linkages', 'All cytidine residues throughout each gapmer are 5-methylcytidines' - and prints the motif '5-10-5' against each of these eight ISIS numbers in Table 4, together with the exact 20-mer sequence. The modifications array is populated from that stated legend plus the printed sequence, one row per position, nucleobase taken from the sequence; the basis field on every row names the legend and the Table 4 line. Position 20 has no 3' internucleoside linkage and is recorded NOT_APPLICABLE. If the project's rule is that only an explicit per-position typographic convention qualifies, drop this array - the measurements and oligos do not depend on it.

ON-TARGET vs UNINTENDED. These are TTR-targeting gapmers; transthyretin is not a coagulation factor and none of these compounds is designed to alter clotting. on_target_effect is therefore false on every row and unintended_toxicity is true on every row, flagging the readout as belonging to the unintended/class-effect safety panel. That flag marks what the row is about; it is not a claim that toxicity was demonstrated on any individual row - magnitude lives in effect_vs_control.

CMC SILENCE. No purity, purity method, identity confirmation or synthesis platform is reported for any compound anywhere in this patent (searched for HPLC, mass spectrometry, purity, purified, endotoxin, lyophilized). Those fields are NOT_REPORTED throughout and that is genuine source silence.

ALIAS CAUTION. ISIS 420915's sequence and chemistry match the compound publicly known as inotersen (IONIS-TTRRx). That identification is external curator knowledge, NOT something this patent states, so the aliases field is NOT_REPORTED and the annotation is confined to the oligo's notes, flagged for re-verification.
refused_rows:
1. PLATELET COUNTS (Table 80, 'Effect of antisense oligonucleotide treatment on hematologic parameters in cynomolgus monkeys', US9061044.txt line 18022, and the equivalent rodent hematology tables at lines 10925, 11034, 12062, 14854, 15504). Platelet counts are printed for the same monkeys in the same study and would have been easy yield, but the patent never links them to any coagulation-cascade readout - Table 80 sits in an inflammation subsection, the coagulation subsection is separate, and no sentence connects the two. Per the endpoint definition, platelet count alone is the thrombocytopenia endpoint and belongs in that dossier, not this one. Not extracted.

2. PROSE-DERIVED no_change ROWS FOR PT / aPTT / FIBRINOGEN. It would have been possible to emit three tidy absence rows reading effect_direction 'no_change' on the strength of the sentence 'PT, aPTT and fibrinogen were not significantly altered'. Refused: for aPTT and fibrinogen that sentence is contradicted by the patent's own tables, so such rows would inject exactly the false negative this bundle exists to catch. The sentence is instead preserved verbatim in severity_stated_by_source on all 126 numeric rows.

3. ANY COAGULATION ATTRIBUTION FOR THE THREE ILLNESS WITHDRAWALS (ISIS 420955 whole group day 31; one ISIS 420957 animal day 44; one ISIS 420950 animal day 76). The patent gives no cause of illness and no bleeding, haemorrhage or thrombotic event anywhere in the document. No bleeding_outcome or thrombotic_outcome row was written. The temporal and rank coincidence with the longest aPTT groups is recorded in extraction_notes as an observation for reviewers, not as data.

4. STATISTICAL OR SIGNIFICANCE CLAIMS. Tables 86-88 print group means with no SD, SEM, per-timepoint n or test. No p-value, no significance call and no severity grade was manufactured; effect_direction records only the sign of the difference between two printed means.

5. A DEFINED BASELINE FOR THE '0 hr' COLUMN. The 0 hr values are extracted as printed at timepoint '0 hr', but no row treats 0 hr as a pre-dose or treatment-naive baseline and no within-animal fold-change over 0 hr was computed, because the patent never defines what 0 hr is relative to. All comparisons are to the concurrent PBS group.

6. A STUDY DAY FOR THE TIME COURSE. Day 84/86 could be back-calculated from 'Terminal sacrifices... on day 86, which was 48 hours after the last dose', and it would have made the rows look more complete. Refused as inference; exposure_duration says the study day is NOT_REPORTED.

7. ISIS 420955 COAGULATION VALUES. None exist in the document. Recorded as three explicit reporting-silence rows (readout_value NOT_REPORTED) rather than being omitted, so the gap is visible; no value was carried over from any other group or timepoint.

8. RODENT CLOTTING TIMES. The mouse and rat tolerability examples measure hematology and chemistry but no clotting times at all. No rows were written for them - a whole-example silence is described in extraction_notes rather than expanded into hundreds of empty rows.
